newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's NSE to launch futures contract by year end.
newsitem.headline: India's NSE to launch futures contract by year end.

text.p: India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) plans to introduce a stock index futures contract by the end of 1996, an exchange official said here on Saturday.
NSE vice president Raghavan Putran told a conference on Asia-Pacific equity markets that the exchange would launch a contract linked to the 50-stock NSE index by year end.

"I think there would be a lot of interest in a futures segment. Indian brokers are used to taking positions on the longer term, so conceptually, they are used to trading on futures," Putran told Reuters after the conference.
He said the exchange also planned to introduce stock options by the middle of next year.
Putran said the current slump in the Indian stock markets was merely part of a "bear phase" that would not be sustained as economic growth and corporate performance remained strong.
High interest rates and the depressed equity market had spurred investor interest in the Indian bond market, resulting in several successful corporate bond issues, he said.
"Eventually, you need to have a developed bond market...," he said. "In India, the asset base is very large but there isn't much trading. So this is a healthy development."
Putran said India's 21 regional stock exchanges were undergoing a process of consolidation, with some of the smaller exchanges grouping together.
He said market forces would ultimately determine the number of stock exchanges in India.
The two-year-old National Stock Exchange has 950 members in over 50 Indian cities trading 1,300 equities and 450 debt securities.
Turnover on its equities market averages $350 million daily, while about $30 million worth of debt securities are traded per day on average, Putran said.
